one_month_reasoning: No MDB earnings in the window (Q3 FY27 reports early December). The CEO exit (announced 9/28), Investor Day (9/29) and the cooler 9/30 PCE print that cut October hike odds are all in the $356 close. In-window: sell-side digestion of Investor Day, unscheduled CEO-search headlines (a permanent-CEO name would be positive; further executive exits negative), the Oct 27-28 FOMC and late-October hyperscaler results. The job board shows 398 open roles updated 9/30, so no sign of a hiring freeze after the CEO exit. These are roughly symmetric; I keep a median of ~$357 (tiny post-overreaction drift) and ~16.5% monthly log sigma, between a calm ~14% and realized 71%/3.5 = ~20% (inflated by two event jumps).

fair_value.method: Blend 40/40/20 of EV/sales (NTM revenue $4.12B x 7.5x + $2.6B net cash, /85M = $394), P/E (NTM EPS $9.9 x 39x = $386) and FCF yield (FY29 FCF $0.95B at 3.5% + cash = $350) = ~$382.

bear.story: March 2027 FY28 guide comes in below ~18% (the FY27 guide already implies Q4 +14-16%), Atlas slides toward 20% as Postgres/DocumentDB take new workloads (npm share of Node DB-driver downloads halved in a year), the CEO search drags or go-to-market leaders leave; EV/sales compresses to ~5x on ~$3.9B.

base.story: Ittycheria steadies execution, MDB keeps beating its guide, a permanent CEO is named in H1 2027, revenue ~20% and +150bp margin; NTM EPS ~$9.9 at ~39x, ~7.5x sales.

bull.story: AI/agentic workloads keep Atlas near 28-30% and total growth mid-20s, margins expand faster, and a strong CEO hire re-rates the stock toward 10x sales, near the upper sell-side targets.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$245 (-31%, ~5.5x NTM EV/sales on ~$4.1B, back in the Mar-Apr 2026 low zone), the price would most likely mean the Investor Day 20%+ framework broke: an FY28 guide well under 18%, Atlas decelerating toward 20%, or a go-to-market exodus during the CEO search, rather than ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Round 2. Supervisor fact-checks I adopt: net cash at Sep-2027 is ~$2.6B with ~85M diluted shares (my $3.1B double-counted the buyback); the buyback has $1.354B remaining; the FY27 guide implies Q4 growth of only +14-16% ahead of the March FY28 guide, balanced by MDB's ~5% beat of its Q2 guide; NTM EPS ~$9.9 (my $9.8 was fine). I also stop using the Substack '11.4x median EV/S' figure and the Blind/Glassdoor restructuring claims (unverified). Multiples: I cut P/E to 39x (from 42x) for SBC at ~20% of revenue and restrictive rates, cut EV/sales to 7.5x (from 8x), and add an FCF-yield leg ($350). Blended fair value $382 (from $415). Alternative lane, rebuilt on verifiable data: (1) npm registry: 'mongodb' driver downloads ~55M in Sep-2026 vs ~34M in Sep-2025 (+64%) and mongoose +69%, but 'pg' went from ~45M to ~201M (+345%), so MongoDB's share of these Node DB-driver downloads fell from ~43% to ~22%. Downloads are inflated by CI and AI coding agents, but the relative shift matches the SO 2025 survey (Postgres 55.6%, MongoDB ~26%, down 0.7pt). (2) PyPI: pymongo monthly downloads rose ~25% Apr-Jul 2026, so absolute usage still grows. (3) DB-Engines: MongoDB #5, score ~381, down ~3.6 m/m (two sources). (4) Greenhouse: 398 open roles, ~43% go-to-market, updated 9/30, so no hiring freeze after the CEO exit. Effect on the forecast: absolute developer adoption is still growing, which supports the ~20% base case, but relative mindshare loss is real. That justified the lower EV/sales multiple and moved ~2pts of probability from bull to bear (bear 0.27/base 0.50/bull 0.23; mean ~$373). It did not change the median revenue path, since Atlas has held ~29% for five quarters. Ladder: lognormal, median ~$365 and 50% annual vol (below 71% realized, which the two jump events inflate; above a large-cap given the CEO vacuum and the March guide risk), with a slightly fatter far-left tail. P(>=356) = 0.52, down from 0.56.
